nodes.label: Reduced consumption practices

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did consumers indicate changes in their shopping patterns during the pandemic?
nodes.answer: Consumers indicated changes in their shopping patterns based on improved wellbeing and financial benefits from reduced consumption.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_001
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How did COVID-19 related lockdowns impact consumers' fashion acquisition practices?
nodes.answer: The lockdowns forced consumers to break from their daily routines, leading to changes in their habits and practices, such as stopping visits to high street fashion retailers with friends on weekends.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_002
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How did reduced disposable income affect shopping behaviour according to Accenture in 2020?
nodes.answer: Reduced disposable income may lead consumers to spend less on non-essential items, affecting their shopping behaviour.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did the decrease in socializing contribute to changes in apparel shopping habits?
nodes.answer: The decrease in socializing resulted in individuals having more disposable income, which they then spent on garments, leading to a shift away from discount shopping towards purchasing more expensive apparel.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did consumers in countries like India and Iran limit their fashion consumption practices during COVID-19?
nodes.answer: Consumers in countries like India and Iran limited their fashion consumption practices during COVID-19 due to the drastic decline in overall spending on apparel, which forced them to limit their fashion consumption practices and extend impulse purchases to online shopping.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What percentage of individuals reduced the practice of purchasing new clothes during COVID-19, and in which countries were the strongest decreases reported?
nodes.answer: 57% of individuals reduced the practice of purchasing new clothes during COVID-19. The strongest decreases were reported in Iran (72%) and India (77%).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_006
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What were some factors that influenced consumers to spend less on apparel during the pandemic?
nodes.answer: Consumers spent less on apparel due to decreased disposable income, lockdowns, and a reduction in discount and impulse purchases.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the relationship between Covid-19 and consumption patterns in society?
nodes.answer: Covid-19 has altered consumption patterns in society by influencing people's choices, priorities, and spending habits, with shifts towards more sustainable and practical consumption practices observed in response to the pandemic.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_008
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can commercial marketing promote sufficient consumption according to the literature review?
nodes.answer: Commercial marketing can promote sufficient consumption by focusing on promoting the benefits and values of consuming less through various strategies and messaging.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is the habitual component of online consumption an area that has not been investigated as extensively?
nodes.answer: The habitual component of online consumption has not been investigated extensively as compared to offline behaviours because consumers have only recently become more aware of the environmental impact of their decisions while online shopping has been prevalent for a long time.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Reduced consumption practices_qna_010
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What concept does Vladimir ova apply to fashion consumption, and what is the conclusion drawn from this application?
nodes.answer: Vladimir ova applies the concept of living with less to fashion consumption, concluding that 'living with less is a path to happiness' and that fashion needs can be met with a relatively small number of good-quality garments.
